section_summary: The section closes a report on rehabilitating Japan’s oil refineries and begins a later group of records on petroleum supply. A Tokyo despatch forwards a bulletin on oil exploration, while an airgram reports plans to resume refining imported crude. Correspondence with Standard-Vacuum Oil Company concerns sterling payment restrictions on crude-oil bids; a final airgram reports increased domestic production.

subfiles.title: Report on rehabilitation of Japanese petroleum refineries, conclusion
subfiles.about: Assesses refinery repairs, capacity, costs and operating needs.
subfiles.summary: The concluding page recommends concentrating Pacific Coast refining, repairing selected plants and importing crude to reduce costs. It also calls for better accounting, technical advice, reliable electricity and coal-fired boilers.

subfiles.title: Record-copy replacement form for Despatch No. 728
subfiles.about: Designates a copy of Tokyo Despatch No. 728 for central filing.
subfiles.summary: The copy replaces an unreturned original.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 728: Exploration for Oil in Japan
subfiles.from: Acting U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards five copies of a Far East Command bulletin summarizing Ralph W. Stephenson’s oil-exploration report.
subfiles.summary: The despatch forwards Information Bulletin No. 18.

subfiles.title: Airgram A-339: Resumption of Pacific Coast refining
subfiles.about: Relays a SCAP press release on refinery rehabilitation and planned processing of imported crude.
subfiles.summary: The airgram identifies refineries scheduled for repair and outlines crude allotments, operating standards and anticipated savings of about $10 million in the first year.

subfiles.title: Standard-Vacuum letter on crude-oil bids and sterling exchange control
subfiles.from: George F. James, Standard-Vacuum Oil Company
subfiles.to: John M. Allison, Department of State
subfiles.about: Explains how British sterling exchange controls affected American participation in bids to supply crude oil to Japan.
subfiles.summary: James recounts Japan’s invitation for crude-oil bids, Standard-Vacuum’s offers and its discussions with the Bank of England. He reports that British authorities refused arrangements for accepting sterling and urges a policy that lets American oil companies compete for Japanese supply contracts.

subfiles.title: Reply to George F. James
subfiles.about: Acknowledges James’s letter about bids to supply crude oil to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Allison says copies will go to concerned Department offices.

subfiles.title: Airgram A-372: Japanese oil production record
subfiles.about: Reports a postwar record in Japanese oil production during October 1949.
subfiles.summary: The airgram attributes higher output chiefly to newly discovered reserves in Akita Prefecture.
